topics.label: Introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by welcoming students, setting out the core learning outcomes, and outlining the scope of cancer therapies to be covered.

topics.label: Traditional cancer modalities: surgery, radiotherapy, and cytotoxic chemotherapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine standard primary cancer treatments, detailing the roles of surgery and radiotherapy alongside the mechanisms, systemic toxicities, and resistance pathways of cytotoxic chemotherapy.

topics.label: Exploiting tumor-specific biological vulnerabilities and checkpoint defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore therapeutic strategies that target intrinsic molecular vulnerabilities of cancer cells, including hormone signaling dependency, cell cycle checkpoint deficiencies, and DNA repair defects.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and mechanisms of resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the targeting of hyperactivated oncogenic kinases with small-molecule inhibitors, detailing the resulting clinical responses, emergence of drug resistance, and bypass pathways.

topics.label: Monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover antibody-based cancer treatments, focusing on the mechanisms of action, cell-surface targeting, and clinical toxicities of naked monoclonal antibodies and antibody-drug conjugates.

topics.label: Cancer immune surveillance and immunotherapeutic approaches
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics address the biological basis of tumor immune surveillance and explore immunotherapies designed to engage the immune system, including checkpoint inhibitors, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapies.

topics.label: Contemporary challenges, historical trends, and future directions in cancer therapy
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics synthesize broad perspectives on cancer management, discussing clinical challenges, historical survival trends, genomic stratification, and the ethical dilemmas of evolving treatment paradigms.
